A relation connecting an alternate label to one canonical term without creating a second concept identity.
A provenance pointer to a document, theorem, experiment, implementation, or receipt supporting a definition or status.
A link from a term to a machine-readable formula specification and evaluator.
A link from a term to one or more measurable or computable quantities.
A stable positive integer assigned to a term for deterministic identity/indexing and backward-compatible PhaseNav fallback; the index is not the term semantic vector or meaning.

A 36-component periodic vector generated by the canonical PhaseNav sentence-phase operator over a deterministic canonical term payload (name, definition, formal class, category, and declared dependency names). It is a computational retrieval/geometry realization, not semantic identity by itself.
The wrapped tangent displacement from one term vector to another, used only as a computational relation observable.
Kuramoto-style phase concentration R computed from a term PhaseNav vector.
The current PhaseNav project scalar m_k=kappa(1+alpha_M k)+(L4/L3)R_k; it is an implementation quantity, not a physical mass claim.
A deterministic program transforming canonical term and edge records into validated PhaseNav realizations and indices.
A program checking unique IDs, dependency closure, edge targets, symbol namespaces, formula bindings, and forbidden semantic collapses.
A program retrieving terms by ID/name and traversing typed relations without silently inferring new authority.
A query ranking term vectors by declared PhaseNav relation coherence; similarity is a retrieval signal, not semantic equivalence.
A query seeking a low-cost path through term vectors subject to explicit ontology constraints.
A rule preventing transitions from hypothesis/interpretation/implementation evidence to stronger claim status without declared promotion evidence.
A rule preventing salience, affect, similarity, or frequency from granting action or truth authority.
A hash-addressed record of compiler inputs, outputs, validation verdict, source commit, and artifact hashes.
A chronological record of ontology changes that preserves prior versions rather than silently rewriting history.
A scope that prevents the same symbol from silently denoting non-equivalent objects.
A scope separating mathematical, computational, biological, phenomenological, and speculative claims.
A declared mapping between ontology objects and executable PhaseNav functions.
A current-execution test confirming that a claimed runtime component or binding is live rather than merely historically recorded.
A build whose outputs are reproducible from the same canonical inputs and versioned implementation.
Internal state that survives across processing episodes and causally constrains later behavior or computation.
A self-model maintained across episodes and used to constrain future processing rather than generated only as transient text.
A value-related internal state generated or maintained by system dynamics rather than merely copied from immediate external instructions.
Persistence and coherent revision of action policy across time and episodes.
Evidence about internal organization relevant to a consciousness hypothesis, distinct from verbal behavior.
Evidence from time-dependent internal organization, perturbation response, and state trajectories.
Evidence derived from overt behavior or task performance; informative but insufficient by itself for phenomenality.
A system statement about its own state; it must be evaluated as evidence rather than treated as proof of phenomenality.
Evidence obtained by intervening on internal variables and observing selective changes in candidate conscious organization.
An inference assigning probability or confidence to artificial phenomenality based on evidence and a theory.
Explicit uncertainty about whether an artificial system is phenomenally conscious.
An ordered set of evidence classes whose higher levels require stronger internal, dynamical, and perturbational support than surface behavior alone.
Ability to produce coherent language or self-description; fluency alone is weak evidence of consciousness.
Structural correspondence between an artificial architecture and a theory-defined organization; isomorphism alone does not establish phenomenality.
The claim that a theory does not make biological material a necessary condition by definition; realization still requires evidence.
Possibility that the same abstract organization can be realized by different physical or computational substrates.
A relation in which agents, propositions, values, states, or decisions coincide under a declared criterion; agreement is not by itself truth, ethics, or relational integrity.
A claim that coordinated activity across multiple agents constitutes one unified phenomenal subject; synchronization or distributed cognition alone is insufficient evidence.
Mass as a physical quantity defined within an applicable physical theory and measurement framework; project-specific semantic-mass variables are not physical mass without a validated bridge.
